# Research Writing Prompt Catalog

> {{scenario_count}} research-writing scenarios and {{candidate_count}} candidate templates. Each scenario has a primary candidate, and most also have an alternative, with traceable sources and copy-ready text.

> Counts are based on candidate groups; a candidate template may contain several short prompts. Choose one that matches your task.

> Candidate order is an editorial judgment, not a benchmark ranking. Check outputs against your model, materials and venue requirements.

> Each candidate states its provenance: verbatim (matches upstream apart from formatting or typo fixes), adapted (abridged or rewritten, with the upstream section named), or written for this catalog (no upstream counterpart).

> **How to choose**: the primary candidate for `4.x` is the structured version and the alternative is the original one-line quick version. `2.x` and `3.x` support adding `MODE: diff` at the end of the input to get a unified diff instead of a full rewrite.

> **Language**: most prompt texts are in Chinese, and some ask the model to reply in Chinese. The `3.3` and `6.1` primary candidates reply entirely in Chinese; `5.2` has a Chinese output template; `1.1`, `2.1`, `2.3`, `3.1`, `3.2` and `5.1` add a Chinese translation or change log; `4.8` explains its English titles in Chinese; `4.9` writes the section in English but returns its grouping table and placeholders in Chinese; `5.3` and `5.4` expect a Chinese description as input. For English-only output, edit the output lines (change 中文 to English, or delete the Part you do not need), or add a line such as `Reply in English` at the end.

# Maintenance and Contributions

Candidate order is editorial judgment; there is no weighted score or community vote. Rationale is based on the concrete task, the prompt text and observable output differences.

The single source of truth is [`data/prompts.yaml`](data/prompts.yaml). After editing it, run:

```bash
python tools/build.py
python tools/check.py
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [PR template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).
